messages.subject: Predicting churn model using SEM
parts:
I have to trying to model churn using SEM. Following is my theoratical model:


model <- ' # measurement model
Service Usage =~ VMail.Message + Day.Mins +Eve.Mins+Night.Mins + Intl.Mins+Day.Calls+Eve.Calls+Night.Calls+Intl.Calls
Customer Dissatisfaction =~CustServ.Calls
Customer Related Variables=~Int.l.Plan+ Vmail.Plan+Area.Code+State
Switching costs=~Day.callpercharge+ Eve.callpercharge + Night.callpercharge +Intl.callpercharge

# structural model
Churn~Service Usage+Customer Dissatisfaction+Customer Related Variables+Switching costs'

To elaborate, I have some numerical observed predictor variables and some categorical observed predictor variables. I have four latent variables (Service Usage, Customer Dissatisfaction, Customer Related Variables,Switching costs) and am trying to predict churn using them. Now, I have three questions:
  1. How do I pass the observed categorical variables into the model? Currently, I have two categorical variables (Area.Code and State) and two binary variables (Int.l.Plan, Vmail.Plan). I am using the factor function on these variables before passing them into the model. Is this the correct way?
  2. The output that I am trying to predict is a binary categorical variable (Churn). Do I need to treat it using some function as well (similar to how I have treated the observed endogenous categorical variables using factor function) 
  3. Further, I also want to check the prediction accuracy of the model and I am using lavpredict to do that. However, I am not sure how to interpret the results. The prediction I am getting for churn is a continuous numerical value between 0 and 0.8.Is the model predicting the probability of a churn happening ( similar to what R does in logistic and decision tress) ?
Thanks for taking time to answer my questions

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Predicting churn model using SEM
parts:
The lavaan tutorial page on categorical data answers your first 2 questions:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Regarding your 3rd question, lavPredict is for calculating factor scores.  Read the "Details" section of the ?lavPredict help page to see "that this function can not be used to ‘predict’ values of dependent variables, given the values of independent values (in the regression sense)."  Although you could manually calculate predicted probabilities of the outcome given your model parameters and any specified levels of your predictors (including the factor scores provided by lavPredict), bear in mind that the latent variables are not observed.  So the predicted probabilities have additional uncertainty due to factor indeterminacy.  You might want to post this topic on SEMNET to get advice about assessing the predictive quality of a latent-variable model.
